tokyo-metro-map.title: Tokyo Metro Complete Guide
tokyo-metro-map.subtitle: Route Map x Transfer Tips x 24H Ticket Calculator | Full Version

sections.body:
[OK] Tokyo Metro has 13 lines (9 Tokyo Metro + 4 Toei Subway) with 286 stations
[OK] Average daily ridership: over 10 million
[OK] Fares are distance-based, NOT flat rate
[!] IMPORTANT: Tokyo Metro is NOT a single-ticket system like London Underground

Main Lines:
* Ginza Line: Shibuya - Asakusa (oldest line)
* Marunouchi Line: Ogikubo - Honancho
* Hibiya Line: Nakameguro - Kitasenju
* Tozai Line: Nakano - Nishifunabashi
* Chiyoda Line: Ayase - Yoyogiuehara
* Yurakucho Line: Wakoshi - Shinkiba
* Hanzomon Line: Shibuya - Oshiage
* Namboku Line: Meguro - Akabaneiwabuchi
* Fukutoshin Line: Wakoshi - Shibuya

Toei Subway Lines:
* Asakusa Line: Nishi-Magome - Oshiage
* Mita Line: Meguro - Nishi-Takashima
* Shinjuku Line: Shinjuku - Motoyawata
* Oedo Line: Circular line (Hikarigaoka - Tochomae)

[OK] 24H Ticket: Adult Y800, Child Y400
[OK] Regular fare calculation: 3+ rides = break even (Shinjuku-Shibuya Y240 + Shibuya-Omotesando Y220 + Omotesando-Aoyamaicchome Y220 = Y680, 4th ride is FREE)
[OK] Usage limit: 24 hours from FIRST USE, not calendar day
[!] NOTE: JR lines NOT included in 24H ticket (Yamanote Line needs separate ticket)
[!] NOTE: Narita Express, Haneda Express NOT included (need separate ticket)

When to buy 24H ticket?
* Ride 3+ times/day → MUST buy
* Stay in Shinjuku, visit Shibuya+Harajuku+Omotesando+Roppongi → MUST buy
* Only 2 rides → single tickets cheaper
* Mainly JR Yamanote Line → don't buy (JR Pass better)

[OK] Shinjuku Station: World's largest station, 53 exits. Transfer time: 15+ minutes
[OK] Shibuya Station: Hachiko Exit is main exit. Transfer time: 5-10 minutes
[OK] Tokyo Station: Divided into 'Above ground' and 'Underground'. Transfer time: 10-15 minutes
[!] WARNING: Some stations have SAME name but DIFFERENT lines (e.g., 'Tokyo' on different lines)

Transfer Strategy:
* Use IC Card (Suica/Pasmo) for seamless transfer
* Paper ticket users must exit and re-enter (additional fare may apply)
* Transfer time: reserve 5-10 minutes (15+ for large stations like Shinjuku)

Reading the Map:
* Orange = Ginza Line
* Red = Marunouchi Line
* Yellow = Hibiya Line
* Blue = Tozai Line
* Green = Chiyoda Line
* Blue-Green = Yurakucho Line
* Purple = Hanzomon Line
* Teal = Namboku Line
* Brown = Fukutoshin Line

Combination Tickets:
1. 24H Ticket + JR Yamanote Line 1-Day Pass = Y800 + Y750 = Y1550, can tour all Tokyo
2. Narita Airport to city: Skyliner Y2470 (fastest 41min) vs Keisei Main Line Y1050 (70min)
3. Haneda Airport to city: Tokyo Monorail Y500 (30min) cheapest

IC Card Choice:
* Suica (issued by JR East): Green color, can use at convenience stores, vending machines
* Pasmo (issued by private subway): Pink color, identical functionality
* Recommendation: Buy one Y3000 (includes Y500 deposit), refundable before leaving Japan

kansai-pass-calculator.title: Kansai Railway Pass Calculator
kansai-pass-calculator.subtitle: Hankyu x Keihan x Kintetsu x JR Kansai x Kanku Rapid | Full Version

sections.body:
[OK] Kansai region has 15+ railway passes with different coverage, validity, and prices
[OK] Main pass types: JR Kansai Area Pass (1-4 days), Hankyu 1-Day Pass, Keihan 1-Day Pass, Kintetsu Railway Pass (1-2 days)
[!] WARNING: Choosing wrong pass = wasting Y1000-3000

Coverage Comparison:
* JR Kansai Pass: All JR lines in Kansai (includes Kanku Rapid)
* Hankyu Pass: Hankyu Railway only (Osaka-Umeda to Kyoto-Kawaramachi)
* Keihan Pass: Keihan Railway only (Osaka-Yodoyabashi to Kyoto-Gion-Shijo)
* Kintetsu Pass: Kintetsu Railway only (Osaka-Namba to Nara/Kyoto)

sections.h2: JR Kansai Area Pass Deep Analysis
sections.body:
[OK] 1-Day Pass: Adult Y2800, Child Y1400
[OK] 2-Day Pass: Adult Y4600, Child Y2300
[OK] 3-Day Pass: Adult Y5800, Child Y2900
[OK] 4-Day Pass: Adult Y6800, Child Y3400

Coverage:
* All JR lines in Kansai region (includes limited express, but need limited express ticket)
* Kanku Rapid (Kansai Airport to Tennoji/Namba)
* Osaka Loop Line, Sakurajima Line (Universal Studios Japan)
* JR lines in Kyoto (Sagano Line, Nara Line)

NOT Included:
X Private railways (Hankyu, Keihan, Kintetsu, etc.)
X Subway (Osaka Metro, Kyoto Metro)
X Bus (except JR Bus)

Calculation Example: From Kansai Airport, visit Osaka+Kyoto+Nara+Kobe, 4-day trip

Itinerary A (Buy JR Kansai 4-Day Pass Y6800):
Day1: Kanku Rapid Airport→Tennoji Y1060
Day1: Osaka Loop Line Tennoji→Osaka Y190
Day2: JR Sagano Line Osaka→Kyoto Y590
Day2: JR Nara Line Kyoto→Nara (round trip) Y1180
Day3: Osaka Loop Line Osaka→Universal (round trip) Y760
Day4: Kanku Rapid Tennoji→Airport Y1060
Total: Y4840, but 4-Day Pass = Y6800, 'NOT breaking even'

Itinerary B (No JR Pass, use IC card):
Same routes with IC card: Y4840, save Y1960

Conclusion: JR Kansai Pass is BEST for 'ride Shinkansen + limited express' travelers. Normal tourists should use IC card + single tickets.

Hankyu Railway 1-Day Pass: Y700, suitable for 'Osaka-Umeda ↔ Kyoto-Kawaramachi' frequent trips
* Osaka-Umeda → Kyoto-Kawaramachi: Y320, round trip Y640, buy 1-Day Pass saves Y60
* Add 'Osaka-Umeda → Takarazuka' or 'Kyoto-Kawaramachi → Arashiyama' = worth it

Keihan Electric Railway 1-Day Pass: Y600, suitable for 'Osaka-Yodoyabashi ↔ Kyoto-Gion-Shijo'
* Osaka-Yodoyabashi → Kyoto-Gion-Shijo: Y420, round trip Y840, buy 1-Day Pass saves Y240
* Add 'Osaka-Yodoyabashi → Uji' = worth it

Kintetsu Railway Pass: Y1650 (1 day), suitable for 'Osaka-Namba ↔ Nara ↔ Kyoto'
* Osaka-Namba → Nara: Y580, round trip Y1160
* Nara → Kyoto: Y680
* Total: Y1840, buy Pass saves Y190

Combination A (Osaka+Kyoto+Nara, 3 days):
* Day1: Osaka city → buy Osaka Metro 1-Day Pass Y800
* Day2: Osaka-Umeda ↔ Kyoto → buy Hankyu 1-Day Pass Y700 + Keihan 1-Day Pass Y600
* Day3: Osaka-Namba ↔ Nara → buy Kintetsu Pass Y1650
* Total: Y3150, 50% cheaper than JR Pass 4-Day Y6800

Combination B (Kansai Airport in/out + Universal Studios):
* Kanku Rapid round trip: Y2120
* Universal Studios round trip: Y760
* ICOCA card (deposit Y500 + top-up Y2000): Y2500
* Total: Y5380, no need to buy any Pass

hokkaido-packing-list.title: Hokkaido Winter Packing List
hokkaido-packing-list.subtitle: Strategy for -20°C Without Freezing | Complete Checklist x Storage Tips

sections.body:
[OK] Onion-style layering: inner moisture-wicking + middle insulation + outer wind/snow protection
[OK] Lower body MORE important than upper body: warm legs = warm whole body
[OK] Shoes are KEY: waterproof insulated boots mandatory, UGG not slip-resistant enough
[!] WARNING: Indoor heating 25°C - don't over-dress, or you'll sweat and feel miserable
[!] WARNING: Phone battery drains FAST in cold - keep in inner pocket

Temperature Guide:
* -5°C to 0°C: Medium insulation (fleece jacket + down vest)
* -10°C to -5°C: Thick insulation (down jacket + thermal underwear)
* -20°C to -10°C: Extreme cold gear (expedition-grade down + fleece pants)
* Below -20°C: Consider canceling outdoor activities

Upper Body - Inner Layer:
* HEATTECH thermal underwear tops: 2 pieces (Uniqlo recommended)
* HEATTECH thermal underwear bottoms: 2 pieces

Upper Body - Middle Layer:
* Wool sweater/fleece jacket: 2 pieces (can layer for temperature adjustment)

Upper Body - Outer Layer:
* Windproof down jacket: 1 piece (suitable for -15°C, long version warmer)

Lower Body:
* Thermal inner pants: 2 pieces (MANDATORY! Jeans don't block wind)
* Wind/snow pants: 1 piece (Gore-Tex material best)

Head:
* Ear-covering beanie: 1 (ear frostbite most common)
* Scarf: 1-2 pieces (can pull up to cover nose/mouth)

Hands:
* Waterproof touchscreen gloves: 1 pair (touchscreen function mandatory for photos)
* Thin inner gloves: 1 pair (double-layer warmer)

Feet:
* Sorel/Columbia snow boots: 1 pair (waterproof + slip-resistant + insulated)
* Wool socks: 3 pairs (Smartwool recommended)

Accessories:
* Heat packs: 15-20 packs (1 in each shoe + 1 on waist + 1 in palm)
* Lip balm + hand cream: 1 each (air is EXTREMELY dry)
* Sunscreen: 1 bottle (snow reflects 80% UV)

[OK] Clothing: roll into cylinders to save 30% space
[OK] Down jacket: use compression bag to reduce 50% volume
[OK] Shoes: place at bottom (heavy items down, light items up)
[OK] Heat packs: carry in hand luggage (restricted in checked luggage in Japan)
[OK] Change of clothes: carry-on (in case checked luggage is delayed)
[OK] Thermos: pack in suitcase (bring hot water anytime)

What to Buy in Japan (don't over-pack):
* Heat packs: ¥200-300 at convenience stores (available everywhere)
* HEATTECH underwear: ¥1,500-3,000 at Uniqlo (cheaper than Taiwan)
* Snow boots: ¥3,000-8,000 at ABC-MART/Don Quijote (buy if urgent need)
* Lip balm: ¥300-500 at drugstores (DHC recommended)

Mistake 1: Wearing UGG outside → soles not slip-resistant + not waterproof, WILL slip on ice/snow
Mistake 2: Only wearing jeans → completely useless against wind, legs freeze solid in 10 minutes
Mistake 3: Forgetting skincare → air below -20°C is EXTREMELY dry, skin will crack and bleed
Mistake 4: Bringing too many thick clothes → indoor heating 25°C, taking on/off 10 times is annoying
Mistake 5: Forgetting sunscreen → snow reflects 80% UV, sunburn more severe than summer
Mistake 6: Phone in outer pocket → battery dies in 5 minutes at -15°C, keep in inner pocket against body
Mistake 7: Wearing high heels/cloth shoes → double risk of toe frostbite + slipping
